title: Grateful Dead Live at Austin Municipal Auditorium on 1972-11-22
lineage: Dat (Tascam DA-20) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1972 fall show featuring a smoking "The Other One", an epic He’s Gone → Truckin’ sequence and a brilliant Playing in the Band jam.
ai_review.review: Reviewers rave about both the pristine, upgraded soundboard mix and the band’s inspired playing. Highlights include a calm‑intensity take on The Other One, one of the best He's Gone performances of the tour, an expansive 10‑minute Bird Song (Playing in the Band) and a fiery Truckin' → Other One transition. The recording is praised as crystal‑clear with only occasional minor quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are 5‑star, emphasizing superb musical performance and an upgraded soundboard mix; the few minor sound issues do not detract from the overall excellence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Upgraded sound over previous versions; tones praised as clear and crisp. Minor occasional unevenness (e.g., "El Paso") but generally very clean vocal and instrumental mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows He’s Gone → Truckin' → drums → The Other One → Stella; seamless transitions and long, exploratory jams (16‑minute PITB). First set includes solid renditions of Bird Song, Casey Jones, Big River, etc.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia is described as "ripping it up" with sweet a‑capella vocals on Stella and strong lead throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Multiple mentions of great Phil riffs, bass leading the charge in The Other One (12‑minute solo), and backing vocals.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir noted for ripping it up alongside Garcia and his vocal contributions during He’s Gone.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Miller praised for showing his chops during the Playing in the Band jam; keyboards highlighted as a key part of the psychedelic sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Clean drumming noted, with Bill’s drum break after Truckin' leading into The Other One.
